ORAL ORDER 1.
Present petition is filed under Article 227 of the Constitution of India read with section 482 of Cr.P.C. seeking following reliefs :-

"(A) Your Lordships be pleased to issue an appropriate writ, direction or order,
directing the respondents No.3 to conduct the further investigation fairly and impartially in connection with CR no. I-129/2011 and further be pleased to direct the respondent No.2 to monitor the said further investigation as carried out by respondent No. 3 and to submit the report within the stipulated time frame as this Hon'ble High Court may deem it fit and appropriate, in the interest of justice;

(B) Pending admission and final hearing of the present petition, Your Lordships be pleased to stay the further proceedings of Criminal Case no. 3145/2012 pending Diptiben Dhirenbhai Gohel vs State Of Gujarat on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196403165/
1 before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/1931/2017 ORDER DATED: 10/06/2025 undefined Ahmedabad (Rural),
Mirzapur, in the interest of justice;
(C) Your Lordships be pleased to grant with other and further reliefs as may be deemed fit and proper by Hon'ble Court in the interest of justice."
2. While taking this Court through facts of the case, learned advocate Mr.Jasani for the petitioner submitted that facts of the case deserve further investigation of the offence.

sentences.text: It is submitted that case the petitioner is that his mother's signature has been forged upon documents send for registering Nissan Car at Chandigarh.

It is further submitted that the petitioner who has purchased Nissan Car from respondent no.4 has given promise that if the applicant pays part of the amount of registration fee, respondent nos.4 to 6 shall pay remaining amount on discount and the petitioner shall get Nissan Car registered from RTO, State of Gujarat.

It is further submitted that according to promise of respondent no.4 to 6, the petitioner paid amount, however, petitioner was surprised to see that registration of car was issued by Chandigarh RTO, which demonstrate that car was registered by registering authority at Chandigarh.
Upon further inquiry, it was found that respondent nos.4 to 6 have send certain documents to registering authority, Chandigarh with forged signature of petitioner's mother.

Therefore, prima facie case under section 465, 468, 471 of IPC though made out, proper investigation was never carried out and it is not included in charge-sheet which was filed under section 406 and 420 of IPC.

It is further submitted that since Criminal Case has commended against accused before the competent Court, in view of judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Anant Thanur NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/1931/2017 ORDER DATED: 10/06/2025 undefined Karmuse v/s. State of Maharashtra [(2023) 5 SCC 802], only remedy available to the petitioner is to approach this Court to seek further investigation.

sentences.text: 2.1. Mainly on above submissions, it is submitted to allow the petition and direct respondent nos.1 to 3 to further investigate the offence and to place report to the learned Jurisdictional Court of further investigation.

3. Learned advocate Mr.Dave for private respondent objected the petition on the ground that filing of petition is abuse of process of law and there is not contract between the petitioner that Car was to be registered through RTO, Porbander and in absence thereof

, merely on certain words of the petitioner, it cannot be believed that priavte respondents have committed any offence under section 465, 468 and 471 of IPC and therefore, the petition being bereft of merits, deserves to be dismissed.
4.
Learned APP while adopting argument of learned advocate Mr.Dave would submit that no case is made out for further investigation of offence.
5. Having heard learned advocate for both the sides, and having considered record, at the outset, let refer FIR filed by the petitioner.

sentences.text: "On being present in person I hereby dictate the facts of my complaint that I reside at the above mentioned address NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/1931/2017 ORDER DATED: 10/06/2025 undefined along with my husband and kids as well as my parents.
I am running business from my cloth shop named Divyaratna situated near Natraj Hotel, M. G. Road Porbandar.
As I do not have any sibling and as both of my parents are aged, they live with us.
My mother is handicapped since last three years and my father is a heart patient.
Therefore I reside in the aforementioned house of my mother with my husband and kids.
As treatment of my father's heart is ongoing at SAL hospital, Ahmedabad, we have to frequently come to Ahmedabad.
Hence for this purpose, we went to Petal Motocon Pvt. Ltd. in Petal Nissan Pvt. Ltd four wheel car showroom and booked a XTL model diesel car on 30/10/2010.
Rs. 1,00,000/- was paid as booking amount and the car was booked.
The said car was delivered to us from showroom on 3/11/2010.
The value of the car was Rs. 24,72,756/-, for which I made the payment by a transfer from my bank account.

At that time, sales manager Mr. Gaurang Chokshi who was present there informed us that if you want to get this car registered in Gujarat than it would cost three and a half lakhs, out of which you will have to pay one lakh fifty thousand and the company will bear the rest of the amount as a discount.
Therefore we gave Rs. 1,50,000/- cash to Mr. Gaurang Chokshi on the same day and took the delivery of car.
I gave photocopy of my mother's passport and ration card and 1 passport sized photo to get this car registered in Gujarat in the name of my mother Nandbala Hiralal Shah.
Thereafter, we received a temporary passing no. GJ-WOL-10-Q-7499 of the car from Petal Motocon Pvt. Ltd.
Thereafter, at the end of January month of the current year I received registration smart card at my home.
The smart card received was registered with Chandigarh RTO registration no. CHO 1 AF 5150 in the name of Nandbala Hiralal Shah wife of Rameshkumar sector 28 Chandigarh.
Therefore we immediately contacted Gaurang Chokshi via phone.
He told us to come to the showroom in person and after that on contacting him in person by going to aforementioned showroom, Mr. Gaurang Chokshi did not give us any satisfactory reply.
Also, after that, upon meeting Gaurang regularly, he stated that it is not his mistake.
Also, Gaurang Chokshi told us that he will get this car registered in Gujarat if we give another Rs. 1,50,000.
On being told so, I have denied.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/1931/2017 ORDER DATED: 10/06/2025 undefined
Thereafter, on contacting the showroom, I was informed that the said Gaurang Chokshi has left the job.
Upon meeting a Wellington Gunther working in this showroom, he took all the original papers of our car and told us that I will get your car registered in Gujarat.

He said so and kept the original papers with him."
6.

Investigation was carried and charge-sheet was filed against the accused for the offence under sections 406 and 420 of IPC.
The petitioner came out with the case that in some of the documents send to RTO, Chandigarh, signature of mother of the petitioner is forged one and IO has not send the same for FSL.

One petition came to be filed before this Court being Special Criminal Application No.914 of 2017.
However, same has been not pressed by the petitioner.
One another application under section 173(8) was also preferred (Annexure D) in Criminal Case No.3145 of 2012.
Same became infructuous in view of order passed in Special Criminal Application No.914 of 2017.
8. In juxtaposition of above, let examine whether the petitioner has made out case to exercise power under section 173(8) for further investigation.

9. The petitioner intend for further investigation of the offence on the ground that in the document which was send to the Registering Authority, Chandigarh for registration of Nissan Car, NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/1931/2017 ORDER DATED: 10/06/2025 undefined forged signature of mother of the petitioner has been made.
FIR which was registered by the petitioner does not indicate any such allegation, if read on its face and in toto.
In the FIR nowhere it is stated that signature of mother of the petitioner is forged on the papers send for registering Nissan Car.
It clearly mentions that papers belonging to the mother of the petitioner has been obtained and send for registration of Nissan Car to RTO.

However, instead of registering Nissan Car at RTO,
Porbandaer it has been registered at RTO, Chandigarh.
Significantly, FIR was registered after car was registered at RTO, Chandigarh.

Thus, what could be said that the petitioner who initially did not put any allegation under section 465, 468 and 471 of IPC tried to improvise his statement made in the FIR and wants that by way of further investigation certain allegations are tried to be added in the FIR.
Manifestly, the petitioner wants to change entire track from one to another at the midst of trial.

10. Case of the petitioner is that he got documents under RTI later on and therefore, he came to know that signature of mother of the petitioner has been forged on the documents produced at RTO,
Chandigarh.

However, except bald statement, the petitioner has not produced any document to support such allegation in FIR where offence under section 406 and 420 of IPC was alleged and the petitioner tried to circumvent on different consideration.
It is also noticeable that mother of the petitioner has not filed any FIR claiming that her signature is forged.
11. In view of above, the petitioner has failed to make out case for further investigation / fresh investigation in the matter.

In so NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/1931/2017 ORDER DATED:
10/06/2025 undefined far as ratio laid down in the case of Anant Thanur Karmuse (supra) stated herein above, there is no cavil that High Court has power to pass order for further investigation /
fresh investigation as to meet with criteria of fair trial.
However, considering facts of the present case, said judgment would not help the case of the petitioner.

12. For the foregoing reasons, the petition is dismissed.
